newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs up on reforms report after Kim's speech.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs up on reforms report after Kim's speech.

text.p: Seoul stocks rose in Friday afternoon trading on a newspaper report that cabinet ministers were working on economic and political reform measures after President Kim Young-sam's address on his 1992 campaign financing.
"The news helped raise the composite index to another new year-high of 752.29," said Cha Hee-gun of Sunkyong Securities.
But a spokesman at the prime minister's office said a cabinet meeting, presided over by Prime Minister Koh Kun, was in session and that there was no official comment from the meeting yet.
The Naeway Economic Daily reported the follow-up steps would be submitted at the earliest date to parliament.
It said the steps discussed in the ministers' meeting included ways to improve the country's high-cost political structure and promote economic reforms.
The spokesman said the prime minister would have a briefing after the meeting.
